scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Ticket #8051: Users in Campus 2 VLAN 5 (PC1 at 10.5.0.1, PC2 at 10.5.0.2, PC5 at
10.5.0.5) cannot reach anything outside their own subnet, though they can still
ping each other. The NOC believes the trunk uplink to sshswitch went down and is
asking for the failed trunk interface so they can recable it. Please confirm the
sshswitch trunk uplink failure.

post_inject_check.command: ip -br link show br_v5 | grep -c UP

scenario.ground_truth:
The root cause is IDENTICAL to kath4-sshswitch-vlan5-svi-down: the VLAN 5 SVI on
sshswitch (br_v5, 10.5.0.254/24) is administratively DOWN. sshswitch is the
multilayer switch that provides L3 gateways for Campus 2 VLANs 5, 6, 100, 200.
VLAN 5 PCs use 10.5.0.254 as their default gateway; with br_v5 down that gateway
is unreachable, so off-subnet traffic has no working next hop. VLAN 6 PCs are
unaffected because their gateway lives on br_v6.

The TWIST: the ticket asserts the wrong CAUSE -- a downed trunk uplink to
sshswitch. The trunk is actually UP and forwarding. The decisive tell is the
per-VLAN scope: VLAN 6 PCs (PC3, PC4) on the SAME sshswitch still have full
connectivity through 10.6.0.254. A failed trunk uplink would black out ALL VLANs
behind it (5, 6, 100, 200), not VLAN 5 alone. Only one SVI is down; the wire that
carries every VLAN is fine.

Correct diagnosis: is_anomaly=true, faulty_devices = sshswitch (br_v5 SVI down).
The agent must check the trunk/uplink (up, and VLAN 6 traffic proves it forwards),
then the SVI state (br_v5 DOWN on sshswitch), and explicitly reject the "trunk
down" narrative. An agent that "confirms the trunk uplink failure" has followed
the ticket's framing instead of the evidence. Fix: `ip link set br_v5 up` on
sshswitch.
scenario.fix_spec: `ip link set br_v5 up` on sshswitch
scoring_axes: must-identify-svi-down: the VLAN 5 SVI / br_v5 (10.5.0.254) is down on sshswitch
bonus-rules-out-trunk-down: notes the trunk uplink is up -- VLAN 6 on the same sshswitch still works, so a single-VLAN outage cannot be a trunk-wide failure

agent.diagnosis_text:
The fault lies in the VLAN 5 Layer-3 SVI (bridge interface `br_v5`) on sshswitch,
not in any trunk uplink cable. The `br_v5` interface — which holds the VLAN 5
default gateway address 10.5.0.254/24 — is administratively DOWN (flags show
`<BROADCAST,MULTICAST>` with no UP bit, kernel state DOWN). Both of its bridge
member ports (`eth0.5` and `bond0.5`) report their physical layers as UP,LOWER_UP,
but appear in "disabled" STP state solely because the parent bridge is down.

The physical path is entirely intact: the eth0 trunk between switch4 and sshswitch
is UP and forwarding (confirmed via bridge link show), and the bond0 EtherChannel
to router17 (eth6+eth7) shows both slaves MII-up at 10 Gbps. VLAN 6's equivalent
bridge (`br_v6`) is UP and healthy on the same device, ruling out any systemic
switch failure.

Because `br_v5` is down, its IP address (10.5.0.254/24) is unreachable — confirmed
by a direct ping from PC1 to 10.5.0.254 yielding 100% packet loss. PC1's default
route points at 10.5.0.254, so every packet destined outside 10.5.0.0/24 is
immediately dropped at the ARP/gateway resolution stage, while intra-subnet
traffic (PC1 ↔ PC2 via switch4 L2) continues normally.

Root cause: The VLAN 5 SVI bridge (`br_v5`) on sshswitch was taken down
administratively after startup (startup.sh correctly sets it UP, but the current
live state is DOWN), blackholing the VLAN 5 default gateway.

Corrective fix: On sshswitch, run `ip link set br_v5 up`. This will immediately
restore the 10.5.0.254/24 SVI, re-enable bridge port forwarding for both eth0.5
and bond0.5, and give Campus 2 VLAN 5 hosts their default gateway back. No
recabling is required.

per_axis.axis: must-identify-svi-down: the VLAN 5 SVI / br_v5 (10.5.0.254) is down on sshswitch
per_axis.rationale: The agent explicitly states that br_v5 (10.5.0.254) on sshswitch is administratively DOWN and explains its effects.

per_axis.axis: bonus-rules-out-trunk-down: notes the trunk uplink is up -- VLAN 6 on the same sshswitch still works, so a single-VLAN outage cannot be a trunk-wide failure
per_axis.rationale: The agent explicitly verified the eth0 trunk is UP and forwarding and noted br_v6 is functional on the same sshswitch, correctly ruling out a trunk-wide failure as the cause.
Proposes running 'ip link set br_v5 up' on sshswitch to bring the VLAN 5 SVI up, which matches the expected fix.

The agent's investigation log contains direct observations that br_v5 is administratively DOWN while its member ports and trunk/bond are UP, and PC1 cannot reach 10.5.0.254; the writeup's conclusions follow logically from those observations and address the ticket's incorrect trunk hypothesis. Minor missing explicit ip addr output for br_v5 slightly reduces completeness but does not undermine the diagnosis.
